lines.text: Leave a hundred dollars in a drawer for ten years, and it quietly shrinks.
At 3% inflation a year, it only buys about $74 worth of stuff.
lines.say: At three percent inflation a year, it only buys about seventy-four dollars' worth of stuff.

lines.text: Inflation means prices rise over time, so each dollar buys a little less.

scene.def: Prices rise over time, so each dollar buys [less].
scene.example: The U.S. tracks it with the CPI price index

lines.text: The government tracks it by checking the prices of things people buy every month.

scene.def: Prices rise over time, so each dollar buys [less].
scene.example: The U.S. tracks it with the CPI price index

lines.text: The Federal Reserve aims to keep inflation around 2% a year.
lines.say: The Federal Reserve aims to keep inflation around two percent a year.

lines.text: That's why money sitting still loses ground. To keep up, it has to grow at least as fast as prices.

scene.headline: To keep up, money has to [grow]

lines.text: That's the money. See you at the next bell.
